Parking the roadmap now. Stage 2 and the three Ranked-list items (O2, O3, O4) each become one deferred item. The roadmap then moves to `specs/completed/`, marked `PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete`.

First, the deferred-item schema and the current backlog:

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/references/deferred-backlog.md
Read specs/deferred_items.md        # may not exist yet
```

Next, append this section to `specs/deferred_items.md`, creating the file if needed. I'll adjust field names to whatever that schema requires:

```markdown
## lock-closures — 2026-11-06

Parked: canal study funding ended. Roadmap: specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md.

- [ ] Closure notices: boat operators get an email within an hour of a lock closing (roadmap Stage 2, Track B, O5).
      Consumes the closure log's live feed; produces a notice job and an operator mailing list. Text-message notices were already out of scope.
      Size: small (one closure-log poll every 10 minutes; spec fully determines it, route to writing-plans)
      Done when: in a test, an email reaches every address on the mailing list within an hour of a new closure entry.

- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock from the river-level forecast (Track A Ranked list #1, O2).
      Builds on Stage 1's response curve (specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md: steep rise above a 3.1 m gauge level).
      Size: small (one model run a day; Stage 1's fit took 22 min on a laptop)
      Done when: a daily 7-day closure-risk outlook exists for each lock from the river-level forecast, with its measured run cost recorded in a findings file.

- [ ] Per-lock closure curves for all 14 locks, pooled across locks (Track A Ranked list #2, O3).
      Stage 1 found the four longest-record locks share close to the same curve.
      Size: medium (about 14 × Stage 1's 1.8 GB, so roughly 25 GB)
      Done when: a closure curve exists for each of the 14 locks, fit pooled across locks on real data, with its measured run cost recorded in a findings file.

- [ ] Closure-history map for the canal's boat operators (Track A Ranked list #3, O4).
      Size: about a day (one static map page)
      Done when: boat operators can open a map page showing each lock's closure history.
```

Then retire the roadmap and commit on `main`:

```
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
# add under the title:  > PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete. Remaining work: specs/deferred_items.md, "lock-closures — 2026-11-06".
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap (funding ended): 1 of 2 stages complete; remaining work to deferred_items"
```

Two notes:
- **Stage 1's findings stay put.** `specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md` and plan 4 remain where they are, and the deferred items point at them. There are no methodology or critique files to retire, because this roadmap had no spec.
- **Stage 2 is parked too, as you asked.** If the notices are ever wanted on their own, apart from the study, that item can be picked up from the deferred backlog without the rest of the study.

Nothing is handed off. The roadmap is closed once the commit lands.
